answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a stake that is slashed if peers prove it lied or duplicated work. Like a falcon that must return to the same perch, an agent cannot wander freely between fresh identities without abandoning its bonded history, and a gale of cheap new accounts cannot wash away that cost because each identity must pay again. Attackers therefore face a rising bill per fake, while honest agents keep one long-lived record.
